hints: Focus on the word growing. A young expanding leaf is still building itself, but it is also green and starting to photosynthesise, so ask yourself if it only imports or can also export.

Remember the definitions: a source is a net exporter in the phloem and a sink is a net importer. A leaf can switch roles as it matures and as the plant's needs change for both sucrose and amino acids.
walkthrough:
**Recall what source and sink mean**

Think like the plant. A source gives out more than it keeps, so it loads sucrose and amino acids into phloem for export. A sink takes in more than it gives out, so it unloads them for growth or storage.

A single organ is not fixed forever, it depends on supply and demand.

**Apply this to sucrose in a growing leaf**

A very young growing leaf cannot photosynthesise enough for its own rapid growth, so it imports sucrose and acts as a sink. As it expands and greens up, it photosynthesises more and can export surplus sucrose, so it acts as a source.

That means a growing leaf can be both, depending on its stage.

**Apply this to amino acids in a growing leaf**

A growing leaf needs lots of amino acids to make new proteins and enzymes, so it imports them and acts as a sink. At other times it can break down old proteins or make amino acids and export them in phloem to younger leaves, seeds or buds, so it acts as a source.

That means for amino acids too, it can be both source and sink. This matches row D.

options.A: Incorrect because amino acids are not sinks only. A growing leaf imports them for growth but can also export them when remobilising protein.
options.B: Incorrect on both sides. It wrongly fixes amino acids as sinks only and sucrose as sources only, ignoring that young leaves import sucrose.
options.C: Correct for amino acids but incorrect for sucrose. Growing leaves are not sources only for sucrose, young expanding leaves are important sinks.
options.D: Correct because a growing leaf can switch roles. It acts as a sink when importing for growth and as a source when exporting surplus sucrose or remobilised amino acids.
